scenes.title: Cold open
on_screen: Title card: Gojinjo Taiko · Japan · 16th century

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The tradition dates to 1577, when the warlord Uesugi Kenshin invaded Noto Province.
Unarmed villagers used war drums and devil masks made of seaweed and bark to scare off the invaders.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: The dance serves as a commemorative cultural heritage practice, reflecting the historical defense of Nafune village.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The music is characterized by the low sound of drums, which is associated with the rumbling of the earth.
The sound is defined by low-frequency drum beats intended to mimic the rumbling of the earth.
